Also registry_win.cpp:696-705. Proposed: widen the rollback owner to the whole write, emit a fixed-literal best-effort exception audit line for the three mutators, correct the three false sentences and audit-log.md:171, add CH-1 tests. independent: security-guardian only (unhappy-path, compliance and chaos were shown SG-1).

trigger: a second writer puts a value into a key the creating walk just made, then the write fails and rolls back

trigger: set_value / delete_value over a secret-bearing registry value; the audit row carries its raw bytes (256 at most) to every AuditLog:Read and Response:Read holder
classification_rationale: audit controls are disclosed but the old=/new= hex carries any value with no filter or recorded owner acceptance
summary: Gate 7 B3 = SG-3 + CO-1 (compliance-officer native HIGH). old=/new= carry hex of ANY value; readers include the legacy /events stream (server/core/src/legacy_events_routes.cpp:20) with no RBAC scoping; 365-day audit retention, 90-day response store, data_hex also in executions.parameter_values. Documented in README:206,242 but disclosure is not a control and no recorded owner risk acceptance was found. A read-time redaction precedent exists (AuditStore::sanitized_detail, audit_store.cpp:657). Needed an owner ruling: (a) agent-side redaction, (b) server read-time redaction (new surface, split), (c) recorded owner risk acceptance. #6298 says the emitting change owes this decision.

trigger: server upgrade ships the 1.1.0 definitions; a registry 1.x agent receives a data_hex-only set_value, writes an EMPTY REG_SZ over the value and answers status|ok

summary: Gate 7 B4 = PD3 (+ER1, CH-8). minAgentVersion is stored and exported, never compared at dispatch; typed values are stored as REG_SZ and answer ok; REG_DWORD with data_hex throws. Disclosed in four places; the real fix (a server-side plugin-version dispatch gate) is out of scope. Options put to the owner: (a) accept as a documented residual and file the gate issue (P1, not roadmap: I2/I3), or (b) re-cut and hold data_hex and the five new types out of this change. Also docs/user-manual/upgrading.md:503-529, content/definitions/registry.yaml:317,511, README caveat 3.

trigger: a command parameter containing an embedded NUL truncates a key, name or value at the NUL before the plugin sees it
classification_rationale: plugin NUL validators are unreachable because params arrive as C strings
summary: Gate 7 B6 = UP-2 (CH-11). Registry-agnostic platform mechanism (agent.cpp:4071 v.c_str(); sdk/include/yuzu/plugin.hpp:43-49). Verified mitigation: the instruction-parameter schema path refuses NUL (instruction_param_schema.cpp:541), so the registry instruction definitions are protected; the direct command route was not found handling NUL (unverified). Exposure partly unresolved for that route. Recommended: record pre-existing with a non-author adjudication after one grep of the direct route, and file the agent-side or route-side guard.

OWNER-OF-THE-CHANGE ACCEPTED, DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL, not a closure and not an independent adjudication. The disposition stays 'open' because the schema has no value for an accepted residual and 'rejected' would be false: the finding is valid. The wording is fixed in 22d2a543e (README, audit-log.md, the routed row and the resource ledger now say the rollback is best effort: a key holding a value or subkey at the check is kept; a write landing between the check and the delete, or over our own same-named value, can still be lost). The compare-before-delete for the same-name case was optional in the governance ruling and is not built; window (a) cannot be closed in code because Windows has no delete-if-empty call.
waiver_rationale: Why an unresolved gating finding is allowed to pass: the check-then-delete window is inherent (Windows offers no delete-if-empty call), the rollback only ever runs on an already-failed create, a foreign value present at the check is kept, and the residual is documented in README caveat 2, audit-log.md and the routed row. Recorded at the derived band; not claimed as resolved.
adjudicated_by: Alex (product owner and owner of this change; NOT an independent adjudicator: the owner of the change recording its own risk acceptance, as the resource ledger Accepted risks section says)
adjudication_rationale: Owner acceptance of a documented residual (resource ledger Accepted risks, B2-R). The separation the de-escalation rule asks for is NOT met: the adjudicator is the owner of the change. Audit trail only; a non-author reviewer who rules on B2-R supersedes this row.
